name: cal-07-hardware-b
version_tag: CALENDAR (shiura 7035937 Ver.2) — tall/small hardware: main-axis, axis-L, bearing-L, click-spring-4copies. FULL SIZE, single colour black, no purge. main-axis is the tallest part in the whole build at 74mm. THIS PLATE IS THE HIGHEST DETACHMENT RISK IN THE BUILD AND WAS QUEUED TO RUN WITHOUT A BRIM — brim_width is 8 here rather than the 5 used elsewhere, and that is deliberate. After cal-03's tall drums let go of the plate and were dragged into a spaghetti mess, every part was ranked by bed-contact-area over height: main-axis scores 5 (380mm2 of contact holding up 74mm) and axis-L also 5 (139mm2 / 25.8mm), against 79 for the month drum that actually failed and 286 for the date10 drum that held. click-spring 20 and nut 23 are also below the failure line. So these are 16x worse than the part that already came off. auto_brim had computed brim_width 0 for this plate because it reads footprint AREA and cannot see slenderness, and the pre-flight audit could never have caught it — brim is not a spec mismatch, it is a spec omission. Do not return this plate to auto_brim. VARIANT CHOICE: plain 'main-axis' and 'axis-L', NOT the -tight versions. The tight pair is the well-tuned-printer option, and this plate already runs xy_contour_compensation -0.06 carried over from the Oechslin work, which tightens fits on its own — stacking both risks a press fit that will not turn. If the assembled axis is sloppy, reprint with -tight and drop the xy-comp to 0 rather than changing both at once. SUPPORTS: enable_support 0, so compose's grounded-check refuses rather than silently printing mid-air; main-axis is the most likely candidate in the set. If it fires, re-spec only that part. Layout: main-axis [90,90], axis-L [170,90], bearing-L [90,170], click-spring [170,170] — smallest bodies here, all >=35mm apart. click-spring-4copies already contains all four springs, do not duplicate it. SPEEDS: stock 0.20mm Standard.
